page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.metal is a bare-metal compute-optimized server built on the ARMv8 64-bit architecture. It features 64 dedicated AWS Neoverse-V1 physical cores operating at 2.6 GHz, with exactly one thread per core and no virtualization layer. Each core has 64 KB L1 data cache and 1.0 MB L2 cache, backed by 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory provisioning comprises 128.0 GB of DDR5 RAM, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio at 2.0 GB per physical core. For high-speed local scratch space and ephemeral data persistence, the server includes 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network interfaces provide a baseline throughput of 30 Gbps, while graphics acceleration is not included.

Benchmark results emphasize strong multi-core scalability and high memory subsystem performance. The bare-metal platform achieves top-decile Geekbench multi-core results, driven by strong software compilation marks using Clang and elevated multi-core stress-ng scores. PassMark memory testing and raw memory bandwidth benchmarks confirm high-throughput data movement across the DDR5 interface, yielding over 277 GB/sec in large uncached read sweeps. Key-value caching evaluations show strong throughput, exceeding 102 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, with similarly high marks in static web serving and database processing. Conversely, single-threaded processing and small-scale LLM generation throughput fall into middle and lower statistical brackets, reflecting an architecture optimized for parallel execution across all cores rather than extreme single-core clocks.

From a workload perspective, the server delivers high resource density for parallel compute tasks that leverage direct hardware access. The combination of 64 dedicated cores, high memory bandwidth, and 3,800 GB of low-latency NVMe storage suits large-scale continuous integration clusters, distributed software compilation, high-throughput web serving, and high-concurrency Redis caching. The absence of a hypervisor eliminates virtualization latency, benefiting latency-critical database engines and real-time processing tasks where predictable core allocation is required.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gd.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server engineered around 64 dedicated physical cores on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture running at 2.6 GHz. Operating without hyperthreading or virtualization overhead, each core pairs with 2.0 GB of memory for a total of 128 GB DDR5 RAM. Hardware resources include a bundled 3,800 GB local NVMe SSD array and a 30 Gbps baseline network link, with no discrete GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, the platform demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing, scoring exceptionally well in software compilation tasks and memory throughput tests, alongside strong performance in Redis key-value workloads and database transactions. Single-threaded metrics and complex large language model text generation show moderate throughput, aligning with its design focus on parallel compute density rather than isolated core bursts. The c7gd.metal configuration is tailored for large-scale software compilation, distributed continuous integration pipelines, high-concurrency microservices, caching layers, and database workloads requiring dedicated non-virtualized access.
